content:
I find several things annoying about our current Archive/Counterexamples build setup:

  1. Their build warnings/errors are silent in their CI step, and instead we need a second build step just to raise the eventual warnings/errors.
  2. Their eventual warnings/errors are raised after linting, even though linting is usually the last thing one wants to do in a PR.

I believe we could solve both steps easily by combining the build of all three libraries into one: Instead of running lake build Mathlib, we run lake build Mathlib Archive Counterexamples. Any objections?

Related: environment linter errors (#lint) on archive or the counterexample are silent right now. (This required adaptations with some linters moving to core, but some of these are really pre-existing.)

I seem to remember that some people (including @Kim Morrison) would like Archive and Counterexamples to use as little resources as possible/not even exist. I suspect the current setup is designed to do so, but I don't really see how exactly this saves resources while I can clearly tell that it costs more of another resource: my time.
So we're planning to split the test+lint job from the build job in #40233 (additional reviews welcome!). Does that PR address your concerns?
